test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 12 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The 11th Fundamental Duty to the Indian Constitution was added in the year __________ by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added to the Indian Constitution by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act** in the year 2002.
 
• This amendment introduced Article 51A (k), which states that it is the duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of 6 to 14 years.
 
• The 86th Amendment Act also made education a fundamental right under **Article 21A** of the Constitution.
 
• The amendment aligns with the objectives of the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The addition of this duty emphasizes the importance of education in national development and individual empowerment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:** These are enshrined in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A. Originally, there were 10 Fundamental Duties added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act:** Passed in 2002, this amendment brought significant changes by introducing Article 21A, making education a fundamental right.
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009:** This act operationalizes Article 21A, ensuring free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• **Education and Development:** Education is recognized as a crucial element for individual and societal progress, contributing to economic growth and social equity.
 
• **Global Perspective:** India's efforts align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4, which aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education for all by 2030.
